mechanism_claims.claim_text: CATH-1(6-26) and ABD1 are the strongest directly bactericidal peptides in the local source, with Table 2 MICs supporting CATH-1 activity across all five tested bacterial strains and ABD1 activity across four strains plus lower C. perfringens MIC.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is direct functional activity, not a structural membrane-disruption assay; exact MIC rows are stored in final/activity_toxicity_evidence.json.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CATH-1(6-26) directly neutralized LPS-induced nitric oxide production in HD11 cells in the Griess assay when peptide and LPS were premixed before stimulation.
direct_assay_types: Griess assay for LPS-induced nitric oxide production
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper discusses possible pathways but does not directly test CD14 or NF-kB binding/translocation for this peptide; those remain inferred mechanisms only.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: ABD1 directly blocked LPS-induced IL-1β mRNA induction in HD11 cells in the qRT-PCR assay and is therefore supported as an anti-inflammatory/immunomodulatory peptide in this source.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The exact upstream signaling pathway for ABD1 is discussed as possible immunomodulation, not directly resolved by the paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: In ovo ABD1 treatment improved post-challenge survival versus PBS control in the yolk-sac infection model, but the paper frames the protective mechanism as likely immunomodulation rather than simply direct anti-E. coli activity.

target_context.challenge: E. coli EC317 yolk sac infection model

mechanism_claims.limitations: Bacterial scores are described as data not shown; no unreported values were invented.
